title: Ahn Se-young seeks 11th title, aims to tie single-season record at Korea Open
text:
Ahn Se-young seeks 11th title, aims to tie single-season record at Korea Open - CHOSUNBIZ 
 2026년 11월 3일(화) Industry Finance Real Estate IT Retail Science Policy Society International Entertainment Culture Sports English Sports Ahn Se-young seeks 11th title, aims to tie single-season record at Korea Open 
 입력 2026.11.03. 09:11 조선비즈 구글 검색 먼저 보기 World No. 1 Ahn Se-young (24, Samsung Life Insurance) will challenge for her 11th title of the season. If she wins, she will match the single-season record for most titles she set last year.
 Ahn Se-young will compete in the 2026 Yeosu Victor Korea Open Badminton Championships, held from the 3rd through the 8th at Jinnam Gymnasium in Yeosu, Jeonnam Gwangju Integrated Special City. Although recent concerns about fatigue and injury raised the possibility of her not participating, she decided to compete and will challenge for the title again in front of home fans.
 The Badminton World Federation (BWF) also drew attention to Ahn Se-young's bid for the record. On the 2nd, BWF said, "World No. 1 Ahn Se-young will lead a stellar field at the Korea Open. The France Open champion Ahn Se-young has already lifted 10 trophies this season. She is only one step away from tying last year's mark of 11 titles," it said.
 Ahn Se-young has a record of 66 wins and 1 loss in 67 matches at international tournaments this season. After losing to Wang Zhiyi (China) in the All England Open final in March, she went on a 50-match winning streak. Her season-winning percentage stands at 98.5%.
 In the France Open final on the 25th of last month, she defeated Pusarla Sindhu (India) to claim her 10th title of the season. Ahn Se-young, who last year topped 11 tournaments to set the joint record for most single-season titles across men's and women's singles, will attempt to match that record again at this tournament.
 The draw has also been confirmed. Top seed Ahn Se-young will face Kaloyana Nalbantova (Bulgaria) in her opening match. Ahn Se-young leads their head-to-head 3-0. If she wins, she will meet the winner of the match between Karupathevan Letsana (Malaysia) and Tonluk Saeheng (Thailand) in the round of 16.
 In the quarterfinals she could face Gungi Riko (Japan), and in the semifinals Miyazaki Tomoka (Japan) is a possible opponent. Miyazaki, noted as a next-generation prospect in Japanese badminton, is 0-8 against Ahn Se-young. In last September's China Masters final, Ahn Se-young also beat her 2-0 (21-17, 21-6).
 A rematch with Yamaguchi Akane (Japan) is possible in the final. Second seed Yamaguchi is placed on the opposite side of the draw from Ahn Se-young, so both players would have to reach the final for the matchup to occur.
 The variable is Ahn Se-young's physical condition. After winning the Denmark Open and the France Open consecutively, she has recently reportedly experienced pain in her ankle and Achilles region.
 Ahn Se-young earlier noted, "I've been running without a break, so I think I need time to regroup now. If my physical condition is still not good, I cannot push myself to compete," mentioning the need for rest.
 Nonetheless, Ahn Se-young chose to compete in the Korea Open at home. Attention is focused on whether Ahn Se-young, who is on a 50-match winning streak, can overcome concerns about her condition and claim her 11th title of the season.
